goal: Implement Step 7 of plan_author_lane_abandonment_lifecycle.md, the completion step: run the full section 10 suites, verify the finished lifecycle live and read-only, fix what that live verification finds, record the final STATUS and the definition of done, and retire the plan's handoff. Live verification found two real defects that the unit suites could not see. First, the claim-identity read ran outside the per-domain failing legs of the flow snapshot, so live claim #2871, titled CLAIM: issue-2870-cutover-columns with no issue number in it, threw out of the map and blanked the entire snapshot: the hourly audit described none of the other seven lanes. The identity read becomes its own failing leg, so one unreadable claim is one unreadable row, reported as unverifiable in both domains. Second, a refusal on --abandonment-audit fell through to the generic handler, which exits 2, and on this command 2 already means an expired author lane was found, so the scheduled run announced every read failure as an expiry report about lanes it never read. A refusal on this command now exits 3, because an instrument that could not read is exactly the unverifiable case and unverifiable outranks expiry. No schema, database or infrastructure change.

prohibited_actions: No database, preview, production, or infrastructure action
No application of the abandonment lifecycle to any live expired claim; the lifecycle is proven by hermetic fixtures and by read-only reporting, never by acting on a real lane
No automatic transition of an expired author claim
No deletion of any coordination ref, claim, branch, pull request, or worktree

No weakening, skipping, or relaxing of any existing check, guard, refusal, or exit code; the exit-code change narrows one command from a wrong code to the stricter correct one and every other command is unchanged
No synthetic review verdict and no self-approval
No new feature; Step 7 is regression, live proof, the fixes that proof demands, and the record
assumptions: A green unit suite is not proof that an instrument works. Both defects fixed here were invisible to 980 passing tests and visible within one live read-only run, because both need a real record that predates the current conventions. The plan's own live-verification gate is what found them, which is the reason that gate exists

Mapping a refusal on --abandonment-audit to exit 3 is a hardening, not a weakening. Exit 2 on this command is a factual claim that an expired author lane was found; a refusal never established that, and unverifiable already outranks expiry in this command's contract. The refusal message is still printed in full, and the generic handler that every other command uses is untouched

Isolating the claim-identity read does not hide the bad claim. It reports it in both domains with the claim number in the message, so an operator is told exactly which claim to go and fix, and the run can never report clean while a claim is unreadable

scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs is the repository's one protected coordination source. Before editing it, the nine open pull requests were checked against the collision rule in scripts/check-pr-source-collisions.mjs and none of them touches that file, so there is no colliding pull request to wait behind
The definition-of-done boxes are ticked against named artifacts rather than from memory, and the STATUS table holds the per-step commits, sub-issues, verdict refs and suite counts behind them
The plan's handoff is deleted in this pull request because this pull request closes #2301, which is what the handoff-contract rule requires; the plan file itself stays as the durable record
